title: Rajamouli Just Launched the Teaser for Fahadh Faasil's Fantasy Film. The Baahubali Team Is Behind It.
excerpt: Don't Trouble the Trouble pairs the Pushpa star with Arka Media Works, a debutant director, and a child with a magic wand. It's releasing in five languages and heading straight to Netflix after theatres.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • SS Rajamouli launched the teaser for 'Don't Trouble the Trouble', featuring Fahadh Faasil.
  • The film is directed by debutant Shashank Yeleti and produced by Arka Media Works.
  • It will release in five languages and stream on Netflix after theatrical release.
  • Fahadh Faasil plays Suri, a character balancing humor and heroism in a fantasy setting.
  • The film aims to deliver a unique cinematic experience, focusing on personal wonder.
A Multilingual Cinematic Experience
›Releasing in five languages: Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, Malayalam, Kannada.
›Global digital premiere on Netflix after theatrical release.
›Targeting audiences in Hyderabad, Houston, and Hounslow.
https://x.com/ssrajamouli/status/2076572508585877735 https://youtube.com/watch?v=RdUPs9e1bUk The man who built Baahubali just handed Fahadh Faasil a magic wand — and the first footage looks like nothing Indian cinema has attempted before. **SS Rajamouli** launched the official teaser for **Don't Trouble the Trouble** on Sunday, and the two-minute clip is already doing what it was designed to do: making you ask questions you can't answer. **Fahadh Faasil** stands atop an ambulance alongside a child wielding what appears to be an actual magical wand, sirens blaring behind them, the sky split between gold and chaos. It's gorgeous, it's bewildering, and it has Rajamouli's fingerprints all over it — even though he's not directing. > **"And with Rajamouli presenting — the man whose visual imagination has grossed over ₹3,000 crore worldwide — even a teaser carries the weight of a promise."** The film is helmed by debutant **Shashank Yeleti**, but the muscle behind the camera belongs to the **Arka Media Works** machine — the same production house that gave the world Baahubali and RRR. Producers **Shobu Yarlagadda** and **Prasad Devineni** are joined by **SS Karthikeya**, Rajamouli's son, who is making his debut as a producer. The family business, it seems, is expanding into new territory. ## Fahadh as 'Suri' — The Role Nobody Expected Fahadh plays **Suri**, a man caught in a world where fortune and catastrophe trade places without warning. If the teaser is any indication, this isn't the brooding, minimalist Fahadh of Kumbalangi Nights or the menacing Bhanwar Singh Shekhawat of Pushpa 2. This is something wilder — a performance that seems to require him to be funny, frightened, and heroic in the same breath. ![Arka Media Works — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/5/5f/Arka_Media_Works.jpg) > "We sought an actor capable of balancing vulnerability with strength, humor with drama," the production team said in a statement accompanying the teaser launch. "Fahadh was the only name on the list." The film also features **Ssara Palekar** alongside Fahadh, and **Saurabh Sachdeva** — the man who terrified audiences as the antagonist in Animal and played Hameed in Pushpa 2 — in a key supporting role. The casting alone suggests this isn't your standard fantasy fare. ## A Five-Language, Netflix-Bound Spectacle Here's what makes Don't Trouble the Trouble especially relevant for the diaspora: it's releasing simultaneously in **Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, Malayalam, and Kannada** across theatres, followed by a global digital premiere on **Netflix**. That means whether you're in Hyderabad, Houston, or Hounslow, this one's coming to your screen.

The music is by **Kaala Bhairava**, whose work on KGF and Pushpa established him as one of Indian cinema's most exciting young composers. Cinematography is handled by **Brad Francis**, and **Praveen Anthony** (known for his work on Vikram) is cutting the film. Every technical name on the roster screams scale. ## Why This Matters Indian cinema has flirted with fantasy before — Brahmastra tried it with mixed results, Adipurush tried it and the internet hasn't forgiven anyone involved — but Don't Trouble the Trouble appears to be approaching the genre with a different philosophy. Where those films chased spectacle, this one seems to be chasing *wonder*. The ambulance. The wand. The child. There's an intimacy in the imagery that suggests the magic here is personal, not planetary. And with Rajamouli presenting — the man whose visual imagination has grossed over ₹3,000 crore worldwide — even a teaser carries the weight of a promise. He wouldn't put his name on something he didn't believe could be extraordinary. No theatrical release date has been announced yet, but with the teaser now out and production wrapped, industry insiders expect a release window in the second half of 2026. Keep your Netflix queue ready.
